thread: Millhaven: source or sink of the contamination

evidence.clue: Sylvanas: ruled south, the lines close; most cross within a mile of the Millhaven crossroads, the rest miss by less than a pen's width.
Jaina's test: if rising there it should be thickest at the crossing and thin evenly along every line going north; if draining in, the lines will disagree in weight and lag.
The staff hummed louder pointed south and climbed as they rode; from the crest every ruled line is drawn to Millhaven; the village is silent: no smoke, no lights, no dogs.

The crossing read at the well: all lines heavy; 'two of them are heavier a long way out than they are under us' (against 'rising'); the two north lines are late by distance (for 'draining in'); the east line does not lag; the west line cannot be heard because the crossing drowns it out. Jaina: 'I don't know... I can't tell you which way it's running.'

The storehouse reads loudest in Millhaven (louder than the crossing) but Jaina will not call it the origin: 'a store is where things end up'. The inn cellar and the mill reads are 'worse than the well'.

At the noon crossing south of Millhaven the mage reads the contamination as 'thicker... Millhaven was a knot. This is... wider. Spread out... It's ahead of us.' Millhaven's role as origin is further doubted by this (the stain continues south).

Chapter 4: in the sick village's granary the staff 'ground' in one long pull; Jaina recalls the Millhaven storehouse, 'the loudest place in that whole dead village': she had said a store is where things end up; 'Here was where it ended up.' Millhaven as sink (where the flour arrived and was stored) now looks likelier than source, but nothing in the prose confirms that Millhaven's storehouse took the same man's flour.

Chapter 5: Millhaven's short-rate loads began at midsummer (first, earliest on the north road, by a fortnight); Jaina's marks are blackest around Millhaven and oldest on the north road. 'It started there, or it started there first. That's not the same.' At the fork her reads cluster on the south road and get older the farther down it goes; she says the contamination isn't (all) in the granaries, 'or it goes in on the road, or at the far end of the road, before it ever gets to Andorhal, and comes round the back.' Millhaven therefore looks increasingly like an early sink, not the source.

notes_chapter5: Leans further toward sink: the far south is older and heavier than Millhaven. Still not resolved on page.
readerKnows: The crossing read was mixed and inconclusive; the storehouse is the loudest but not claimed as origin; the stain is wider and thicker farther south than Millhaven.
povCharacterKnows: Sylvanas: no clean source-or-sink answer; the mage will not guess; she does not conclude grain.
notes_chapter4: Leans toward sink (a place where things end up) after the granary read, but the source of the supply is a man with a cart and a stack built elsewhere (Andorhal stencil: possibly a decoy). Still not explicitly resolved on page.
notes: Still open. 'Millhaven was the first village fully taken' is about the people, not the origin. Do not resolve with a clean answer yet.
